title: pioneer-health-integration-call-notes-2026-04-12
content:
Attendees:
- Pioneer Health: Sarah Kim (PM), Dr. Leo Martins (Clinical IT), Omar Rizvi (Security lead)
- Redwood: Aisha Patel (CS), Miguel Torres (Solutions Eng), Jade Nguyen (SRE)

Meeting goal: Quick alignment on Pioneer Health's pilot integration for clinical summarization and patient messaging; identify security/regulatory constraints, throughput targets, and first milestone for the POC.

Summary / high-level:
- Pioneer wants to evaluate Redwood's inference for two use cases: 1) generating clinical visit summaries (structured + natural language) from EHR notes; 2) patient-facing message generation (appointment reminders and pre-visit instructions).
- Primary constraints: PHI handling (HIPAA), data residency (US-East required for pilot), strict audit logs and retention controls, and an initial latency SLO for patient-facing messages (<250ms 95th p50 less critical).
- Pioneer prefers Redwood Private (VPC) for pilot but is open to Dedicated if governance timeline for Private is longer than 6 weeks.

Requirements (captured during call):
- Data residency: All PHI must remain in US-East region. No logs containing PHI may be persisted beyond 30 days.
- Access control: SSO via SAML + SCIM provisioning; RBAC at route/model level.
- Auditability: Per-request audit logs with request IDs, model version, prompt hash (no raw prompt persisted unless flagged), and operator who triggered replays.
- Encryption: CMEK preferred; HSM/KMS integration required for production.
- Model behavior: Need deterministic summarization baseline for clinician review (configurable temperature=0.0, system prompt templates).
- Throughput: Pilot expected ~50 qps for message generation at peak; clinical summarization asynchronous batch of ~500 documents nightly initially.
- Latency: For patient messages target 95th <= 250ms with fallback path to a lighter model (quantized) under contention.
- Testing: Will provide 200 de-identified example records for prompt tuning/evals; need a safe sandbox with synthetic data first.

Integration gotchas / risks noted:
- EHR vendor (MedSysX) only supports HL7 v2 export currently — will need a small ETL to convert notes into the prompt format and strip PHI for dev tests.
- Pioneer requires that no raw prompts containing PHI are stored in Redwood logs by default; scope and mechanism for storing prompt hashes and selective retention must be explicit in contract.
- Role separation: clinical reviewers must have read-only ability to replay model outputs but not re-run with raw PHI until production is approved.
- Certs & network: Client firewall will only allow TLS outbound via specific egress IPs; for Private deployment we need to coordinate ingress NAT config with their network team (Omar).

Questions that need follow-up:
- Legal: Pioneer legal wants a short template of our SOC2 + HIPAA controls (data flows, BAAs). Need to send within 48 hours.
- Encryption: Confirm whether CMEK + HSM is available during Dedicated pilot or only in Private.
- Billing: Pioneer is evaluating committed Dedicated for predictable cost — need a rough estimate for 50 qps sustained + 500 nightly batch.
- Rollouts: Clarify our canary rollback story for model updates when clinical quality regressions are detected.

Action items / next steps:
- Aisha: Send Pioneer the security pack (SOC2, HIPAA checklist, BAA draft) by 2026-04-14. (Owner: Aisha; due: 2026-04-14)
- Miguel: Draft an integration architecture diagram (HL7 -> ETL -> Redwood sandbox -> clinical reviewer UI) and sample prompt templates; include synthetic-data testing plan. (Owner: Miguel; due: 2026-04-16)
- Jade: Confirm network/egress IP requirements for Private vs Dedicated and whether CMEK/HSM is supported in Dedicated pilot; loop in infra team. (Owner: Jade; due: 2026-04-15)
- Pioneer (Sarah): Share 200 de-identified sample notes and point of contact for EHR team (Omar to share MedSysX contact). (Owner: Sarah; due: 2026-04-17)
- Schedule: Set follow-up technical deep-dive next week focusing on prompts/eval criteria — proposed 2026-04-19 10:00 ET. Aisha to send invite.

Notes / conversation highlights:
- Dr. Leo emphasized clinician trust: we must provide a model-stamped lineage for each summary and an easy revert/rewrite flow.
- Omar asked about our ability to redact PHI at spur-of-moment for diffs; suggested adding an explicit redaction step in ETL before sending to Redwood for dev testing.
- Pioneer is budget-conscious but willing to pilot on Dedicated if time-to-deploy Private exceeds 6 weeks. They want clear thresholds for when we recommend quantized fallback models to meet latency SLOs.

Risks to monitor:
- Contractually required BAA + HIPAA artifacts could delay kickoff by 2–3 weeks if legal review finds gaps.
- If EHR export cadence or format changes, ETL effort could expand beyond estimate.
- Performance tuning (latency under 250ms p95) may require model variant/batching trade-offs that impact cost — surface early in pricing.

Attachments / artifacts to produce for Pioneer:
- Security pack (SOC2 + HIPAA controls + BAA draft)
- Integration architecture diagram + ETL example
- Sample prompt templates + evaluation rubric for clinical quality
- Cost estimate for Dedicated pilot (50 qps sustained) and optional Private deployment premium

Open items for Redwood internal:
- Confirm whether prompt hashing approach (store hash and metadata, not raw prompt) meets Pioneer legal. If not, discuss selective retention plus redact-on-write options. (Owner: Legal/Privacy team)
- Evaluate feasibility of supporting CMEK/HSM during Dedicated pilot; if not feasible, create clear timeline for migration to Private with CMEK.

Status: Draft notes — POC kickoff contingent on legal sign-off and delivery of sample records.
